stem:
Meera's mother uses a shiny steel ladle in the kitchen. Meera looks at the inside of the ladle's bowl, where her face appears magnified and upright when she holds it close. The inside of the bowl is the reflecting surface, and it curves inwards like the inside of a spoon.
Which type of spherical mirror does this reflecting surface behave like?

options.text: a convex mirror, because the surface bulges outwards towards her face
a concave mirror, because the reflecting surface curves inwards
a plane mirror, because the steel surface is smooth and shiny
a convex mirror, because all shiny metal objects behave as convex mirrors

teacher.key_rationale: The reflecting surface (inside of the bowl) curves inwards, so it acts as a concave mirror; inward-curving reflecting surfaces are concave by definition. Option A is the trap for students who focus on the outer bulge of the ladle instead of which surface actually reflects.
